Action: For decades, investors looked to the Federal Reserve for clues about where markets were headed. Today, they are increasingly watching Washington as well. Writing for The National, Tim Fox explores whether investors have started pricing in a so-called 'Trump put' — the belief that the White House may adjust its approach on issues such as tariffs or geopolitics if market pressure becomes too intense. The broader lesson is that, in today's markets, investors must also monitor tariff negotiations, diplomatic developments and presidential commentary
